causes: Variable is out of scope (declared in a different block)
WJ0001.explanation: The compiler cannot find a variable with this name in the current scope. This usually means the variable hasn't been declared yet, or it's out of scope.
solutions: Check the spelling of the variable name
Declare the variable before using it: let x = 42
Make sure the variable is in scope
WJ0001.title: Variable not found

WJ0002.explanation: The compiler cannot find a function with this name. This might be because the function hasn't been defined, or the module containing it hasn't been imported.
solutions: Check the spelling of the function name
Define the function before calling it
Import the module: use std::collections::HashMap
WJ0002.title: Function not found

WJ0003.explanation: The compiler expected one type but found another. In Windjammer, types must match exactly. You may need to convert between types explicitly.
solutions: Use .parse() to convert string to number: "42".parse()
Use .to_string() to convert number to string: 42.to_string()
Check the function signature for expected types
WJ0003.title: Type mismatch

causes: Trying to modify an immutable variable
WJ0004.explanation: Variables in Windjammer are immutable by default. To modify a variable, you must declare it as mutable using 'let mut'.
solutions: Declare the variable as mutable: let mut x = 42
Create a new variable instead of modifying the existing one
WJ0004.title: Cannot modify immutable variable

WJ0005.explanation: The compiler cannot find a type with this name. This might be a typo, or the type might be defined in a module that hasn't been imported.
solutions: Check the spelling of the type name
Define the type (struct, enum, etc.)
Import the module containing the type
WJ0005.title: Type not found

causes: Module not in the correct directory
WJ0006.explanation: The compiler cannot find a module with this name. Check that the module exists and is in the correct location.
solutions: Check the spelling of the module name
Create the module file
Check the module is in the correct location
WJ0006.title: Module not found

causes: Value passed to function that takes ownership
Auto-clone system couldn't insert clone automatically
WJ0007.example:
// Usually handled automatically, but if not:
let data = vec![1, 2, 3]
process(data.clone())  // Explicit clone
println!("{}", data.len())
WJ0007.explanation: This value was moved to another location and can no longer be used here. In Windjammer, most values can only be used once unless they implement Copy. However, the auto-clone system should handle most cases automatically.
solutions: Use a reference (&) instead: process(&data)
Clone explicitly: process(data.clone())
Restructure code to avoid multiple uses
WJ0007.title: Value was moved

causes: Mutable borrow while immutable borrow exists
WJ0008.explanation: You're trying to borrow a value as mutable, but it's already borrowed as immutable, or vice versa. Windjammer enforces Rust's borrowing rules to ensure memory safety.
solutions: Ensure borrows don't overlap in scope
Use only one mutable borrow at a time
Restructure code to avoid conflicting borrows
WJ0008.title: Cannot borrow as mutable

WJ0009.explanation: When creating a struct, you must provide values for all fields.
solutions: Add the missing field
Check field names match struct definition
WJ0009.title: Missing field in struct

WJ0010.explanation: Your match expression doesn't cover all possible cases. Windjammer requires all patterns to be handled for safety.
solutions: Add missing match arms
Add a wildcard pattern: _ => ...
WJ0010.title: Pattern match not exhaustive

causes: Calling a method that changes the value (`push`, `insert`, a method that changes `self`)
WJ0051.explanation: A local binding (`let`, a `for` loop variable) is immutable unless declared `mut` (ADR-0002). The program assigns to it, assigns to a field or element of it, calls a method that changes it, or passes it to a function that changes it. `wj fix` adds the `mut`.
solutions: Declare the binding `let mut x` (`let (mut a, b)`, `for mut x in`)
Run `wj fix <path>` to insert every missing `mut`
WJ0051.title: Local binding changed but not declared mut

causes: Returning a scratch string or a handle of a local arena
Pushing an arena value into a collection that outlives the arena
WJ0160.explanation: A value allocated in an arena (`Arena::alloc`, `Scratch::str`, `new_string`, `new_list`) is used where it would outlive the arena: returned from the function that declares the arena, stored in a variable, field or collection declared outside the arena's scope, used as the value of the block that declares the arena, or used after the arena's `reset()`.
solutions: Copy the value out (`.to_string()`, `.to_vec()`) before the arena goes away
Declare the arena in the caller and pass it in
Allocate again after `reset()`, or use `try_get` for a handle that may be stale
WJ0160.title: Arena value escapes its arena

causes: `use std::arena` with a compiler built without `unstable_arenas`
WJ0161.explanation: Arenas (ADR-0025) are behind the compiler feature `unstable_arenas`.
solutions: Build the compiler with `cargo build --features unstable_arenas`
WJ0161.title: `std::arena` is unstable

causes: A value read from a file, standard input or a request is interpolated into the command of `process::run`
Such a value names the file `fs::write` writes, or is concatenated into the SQL text of `query`/`execute`
WJ0173.explanation: Data the program did not produce (file contents, standard input, an HTTP request, a database row) flows into a command, the path of a file write or SQL text without passing through a sanitizer (ADR-0009). The environment and the command line belong to the operator and are not sources. `wj check`, `wj build` and `wj run` stop on it.
solutions: Pass the program and its arguments separately: `process::run_with_args(program, args)` uses no shell
Use SQL placeholders (`$1`, `?`) and pass the value in `params`; keep one path component with `path::file_name(..)`
Validate in a function documented `/// wj-taint: sanitizer`; a reviewed function may be documented `/// wj-taint: trusted(<reason>)`
WJ0173.title: Untrusted data reaches a command, file path or query

causes: A `spawn` used as a statement outside a `scope { }`
A task bound to a name nothing uses
WJ0190.explanation: Every task (`spawn`, `async`, or a call returning `Task<T>`) is waited on: inside a `scope { }`, which waits for it, or through `.wait()` (ADR-0004).
solutions: Wrap the work in `scope { ... }`
Keep the task and call `.wait()`
WJ0190.title: Task is never waited on

WJ0191.explanation: `thread { }`, `ch <- v` and `<-ch` were removed by ADR-0004: write `spawn { }`, `ch.send(v)` and `ch.recv()`; `wj fix` rewrites them.
solutions: Run `wj fix <path>`
WJ0191.title: Removed concurrency syntax

causes: `spawn { total += x }` with `total` a local of the enclosing code
WJ0192.explanation: A task works on its own copy of the variables it reads; an assignment to one inside the task is refused (ADR-0004).
solutions: Return the value and read it with `t.wait()`, or send it on a channel
WJ0192.title: Task changes a captured variable

WJ0193.explanation: A `spawn` task captures a value bound to its thread (`Rc`, `RefCell`, `Cell`, `Weak`); use `async` or build the value inside the task (ADR-0004).
solutions: Start the task with `async`
Build the value inside the task
WJ0193.title: Value cannot move to another thread

causes: `adapters::serve` where `serve` is declared in `adapters::http` and `adapters` has no `pub use http::serve`
WJ0194.explanation: A path or import names an item through a module that only gets it from one of its child modules; `pub mod child` re-exports nothing, a module re-exports a name only through an explicit `pub use` (ADR-0040).
solutions: Add `pub use http::serve` to the re-exporting module (`wj fix` does)
Name the item by its declaring module: `adapters::http::serve`
WJ0194.title: Name is not re-exported

causes: A misspelled builtin such as `normalise`, or a helper that was never defined
WJ0195.explanation: A WJSL shader calls a name that is not a WGSL builtin, a value constructor, a struct or a function declared with `fn` in the shader; reported at build time instead of failing later in the WGSL validator.
solutions: Correct the spelling (the diagnostic names the closest builtin or user function)
Define the function with `fn` or import the file that defines it
WJ0195.title: Undefined shader function

causes: A `#` comment or directive, or a stray symbol
WJ0196.explanation: A WJSL shader contains a character the lexer cannot tokenize, most often a line starting with `#` (WJSL has no `#` comments); it used to end the token stream silently and produce an empty WGSL file.
solutions: Write comments with `//`
Remove the stray character, or use `use "path"` to include another shader file
WJ0196.title: Unexpected character in shader source

causes: `use crate::brdf::fresnel` where `brdf.wjsl` is missing from the folder or declares no `fresnel`.
WJ0197.explanation: A `.wjsl` import `use crate::module::item` names a module file that is not in the entry file's folder, an item the module does not declare, a name that is already declared or imported in the importing file, or uses a form the module system does not support yet (only `crate::` paths into the same folder). The module is the file stem; `crate` is the entry file's folder (docs/design/wjsl-modules.md).
solutions: Create the module file next to the entry file, fix the spelling, or import each name once; import two same-named items through their modules (`use crate::a`, then `a::name(..)`).
WJ0197.title: WJSL import does not resolve

causes: `use crate::brdf::pow5` where `fn pow5` in `brdf.wjsl` has no `pub`.
WJ0198.explanation: A `.wjsl` file imports or calls a function, struct or const that its module does not declare `pub`. Items are private unless `pub`, as in Windjammer.
solutions: Declare the item `pub` in its module; the message names the file and the exact declaration to change.
WJ0198.title: WJSL item is private to its module

WJ0199.explanation: Two or more `.wjsl` modules import each other, directly or through a chain. WGSL has no recursion and a cycle never buys anything; the message lists the chain.
solutions: Move the shared items into a third module that both import.
WJ0199.title: WJSL import cycle

causes: `brdf.wjsl` declares `@group(0) @binding(0) uniform u: f32;` and another file imports from it.
WJ0200.explanation: A library module (a `.wjsl` file imported by another) declares a binding, a `var<...>` global or an entry point, or `pub` is used on something other than `fn`, `struct` or `const`. Library modules hold only functions, structs and consts so that they can run on the CPU as well; bindings and pipeline layout belong to the entry file.
solutions: Move the binding or entry point to the entry file and pass the resource to the library function as a parameter.
WJ0200.title: WJSL module declares something only an entry file may

WJ0201.explanation: A `.wjsl` identifier contains `__`. The double underscore is reserved for module-qualified emitted names such as `brdf__fresnel_schlick`, which keeps those names collision-free.
solutions: Rename the identifier without a double underscore.
WJ0201.title: WJSL identifier contains a double underscore

WJ0202.explanation: A `for` loop over a collection changes that collection in its body (`push`, `pop`, `clear`, `remove`, `sort`, an assignment to `v` or `v[i]`, `&mut v`). `wj run` walks a snapshot and does not see the change; a compiled build keeps the collection borrowed for the whole loop and rustc rejects it.
solutions: Collect the changes in a second list (or the indexes to change) and apply them after the loop
Loop over `0..v.len()` and index `v` when the body has to change it
Write `for p in v.clone()` when the loop should see a snapshot
WJ0202.title: Loop changes the collection it iterates
